vectors.name: a_file_key_adds_a_file_key
vectors.why: A key that counts adds another, and both count at once.

vectors.name: a_file_key_adds_a_passkey
vectors.why: A version 5 adds a passkey, signed here with ES256 by the file key that counts, and by the new passkey's one touch over the same signing input.

vectors.name: a_passkey_adds_a_passkey
vectors.why: A passkey adds another, signing WA256.

vectors.name: a_host_rp_passkey_adds_a_passkey
vectors.why: An owner who signed up on a host's page adds another sign-in there, such as a second phone.

vectors.name: a_host_rp_passkey_adds_a_computers_key
vectors.why: And a computer's key that signs ES256, so an owner with only a phone so far can later sign in on a computer.

vectors.name: a_host_rp_owner_moves_to_another_rp_by_recovery
vectors.why: The recovery code moves an owner from one host's passkey to a passkey at another page.

vectors.name: a_recovery_onto_a_localhost_passkey
vectors.why: Nor does the recovery code move an owner onto one.

vectors.name: a_key_removes_itself
vectors.why: Any key that counts removes any key, itself included.

vectors.name: a_later_key_removes_an_earlier_one
vectors.why: Including the event's own, so a laptop can replace the first computer.

vectors.name: a_recovery_after_an_addition_and_a_removal
vectors.why: The backup overrides every key: only the key it names counts, and its seq counts every statement before it.

vectors.name: a_recovery_to_the_key_left_needs_a_new_sealing_key
vectors.why: A recovery is read against the key the event named, though it was removed, so moving to the added key that's left keeps no sealing key.

vectors.name: a_recovery_committing_to_a_key_the_id_had
vectors.why: A key's name never means the backup, so a device that held a key never holds the backup.

vectors.name: a_recovery_sealing_to_a_key_the_id_had
vectors.why: Nor the sealing key.

vectors.name: a_recovery_dated_past_what_every_reader_holds
vectors.why: issued_at fits a signed 64-bit integer, as every reader can hold one.

vectors.name: a_key_added_after_a_recovery
vectors.why: Keys are added again under the key the recovery named.

vectors.name: an_addition_and_rules_in_one_touch
vectors.why: An addition goes in one touch with other objects, and each verifies alone.

vectors.name: an_id_at_every_limit
vectors.why: An ID at every limit fits under 80 KiB, which is why that's the limit.

vectors.name: added_by_a_removed_key
vectors.why: A removed key signs nothing more.

vectors.name: by_names_no_key_that_counts
vectors.why: A stranger can't name itself.

vectors.name: by_names_one_key_signed_by_another
vectors.why: The signature is checked under the key by names alone.

vectors.name: a_wa256_header_from_a_file_key
vectors.why: A file key signs only ES256.

vectors.name: a_recovery_signed_by_an_added_key
vectors.why: Only the backup signs a recovery, never a key that counts.

vectors.name: a_stand_in_with_a_key_statement
vectors.why: A stand-in's key is on its agent's machine, and no owner has signed for it.

vectors.name: an_addition_without_the_added_keys_signature
vectors.why: A key that counts alone can't add a key: whoever adds one shows they hold it.

vectors.name: an_addition_the_added_key_didnt_sign
vectors.why: The second signature is the added key's, not the signer's again.

vectors.name: an_added_keys_signature_over_another_input
vectors.why: What the added key signed for anything else proves nothing here.

vectors.name: an_added_passkeys_touch_at_a_hosts_rp
vectors.why: An added passkey's touch is for the RP ID its addition names, here another page's, so a touch at a host's name doesn't stand in for it.

vectors.name: adding_the_agents_key_without_it
vectors.why: An agent's key is public, so a thief with one owner key could otherwise add it, remove it and leave a copy under the owner's next recovery. Without the agent's key, which Signet never signs an owner's object with, there's no such copy.

vectors.name: adding_a_key_the_id_had
vectors.why: A key removed stays removed: one point is one key's for good.

vectors.name: adding_the_backup
vectors.why: The backup's holder could sign recoveries and everything else.

vectors.name: adding_the_sealing_key
vectors.why: One key never does both jobs.

vectors.name: adding_a_passkey_at_a_hosts_rp
vectors.why: A computer adds a passkey made on a host's page, where the owner signs in from a phone.

vectors.name: an_added_host_passkeys_touch_from_another_origin
vectors.why: That passkey's touch counts only from the host's own https origin, never a page on the owner's computer.

vectors.name: adding_a_passkey_at_an_ip_address
vectors.why: An RP ID is a name, never an address.

vectors.name: adding_a_passkey_for_localhost
vectors.why: Any program on the owner's machine can serve a page at localhost and have their touch sign what it likes.

vectors.name: a_v4_addition_naming_an_rp
vectors.why: A version 4 adds a file key, and has one spelling.

vectors.name: a_v5_addition_with_no_rp
vectors.why: A passkey signs for one RP ID, which the addition names.

vectors.name: a_key_statement_with_another_version
vectors.why: An addition is version 4 or 5, and v alone names its kind.

vectors.name: a_fifth_key
vectors.why: At most 4 keys count at once.

vectors.name: eight_additions
vectors.why: Removals don't count, so an ID can add and remove 8 times.

vectors.name: a_ninth_addition
vectors.why: An ID adds at most 8 keys between one recovery and the next.

vectors.name: a_ninth_addition_after_a_recovery
vectors.why: A recovery starts the count again, so a thief who spent every addition with a stolen sign-in leaves the owner nothing worse than recovering.

vectors.name: key_statements_up_to_the_room_left_for_recoveries
vectors.why: Every key statement here leaves 1,600 characters for each of the 7 recoveries left.

vectors.name: a_key_statement_leaving_no_room_for_the_recoveries_left
vectors.why: One more would leave too little room for the owner to recover the ID as many times as it still may.

vectors.name: a_removal_leaving_no_room_for_the_recoveries_left
vectors.why: A removal leaves the same room, or a thief with one stolen sign-in could fill the ID removing what it added. A recovery code set later can't come near it: only an ID with no recovery yet sets one, and its 16 key statements at their longest leave room to spare.

vectors.name: adding_a_key_from_before_a_recovery
vectors.why: A key the ID had before a recovery is one it had.

vectors.name: adding_a_point_off_the_curve
vectors.why: A key is a point on the curve.

vectors.name: an_addition_dated_past_what_every_reader_holds
vectors.why: issued_at fits a signed 64-bit integer, as every reader can hold one.

vectors.name: a_removal_dated_past_what_every_reader_holds
vectors.why: Nor a removal's.

vectors.name: removing_the_last_key
vectors.why: At least one key counts after a removal.

vectors.name: a_removal_by_a_stranger
vectors.why: by names a key that counts, so a host can't forge a removal of an owner's sign-in.

vectors.name: a_removal_signed_by_another_key
vectors.why: And the signature is checked under the key by names alone.

vectors.name: removing_a_key_that_doesnt_count
vectors.why: A removal names a key that counts now.

vectors.name: a_removal_typ_with_an_addition_payload
vectors.why: A statement's kind is its typ, and its v is held to it: this would be a removal in every field but v.

vectors.name: fields_reordered
vectors.why: One encoding: the fields in their one order.

vectors.name: removal_fields_reordered
vectors.why: A removal too.

vectors.name: an_unknown_field
vectors.why: Unknown fields are refused.

vectors.name: by_in_capitals
vectors.why: A key's name has one spelling.

vectors.name: an_owner_with_no_recovery_code_yet
vectors.why: An owner ID can be made without showing a recovery code.

vectors.name: recovering_before_a_code_is_set
vectors.why: No backup satisfies a rule set later, so nothing recovers the ID until a code is set.

vectors.name: a_key_that_counts_sets_the_code
vectors.why: A version 7 by any key that counts sets the rule once the person has saved the code.

vectors.name: and_then_the_code_recovers
vectors.why: The backup it commits to recovers the ID as any backup does.

vectors.name: a_passkey_sets_the_code
vectors.why: A passkey signs it with WA256.

vectors.name: setting_the_code_twice
vectors.why: Once: a key that counts can't move a code that's set, or a thief holding one could take the ID for good.

vectors.name: setting_a_code_over_a_backup
vectors.why: An ID made with a backup has nothing to set.

vectors.name: a_code_committing_to_the_ids_own_key
vectors.why: A device that holds a key never holds the backup.

vectors.name: a_code_committing_to_an_added_key
vectors.why: Nor an added one.

vectors.name: a_code_set_by_an_added_key
vectors.why: Any key that counts sets it.

vectors.name: a_code_set_by_a_stranger
vectors.why: by names a key that counts.

vectors.name: a_code_signed_by_another_key
vectors.why: And the signature is checked under the key by names alone, or a host could commit the ID to a backup of its own.

vectors.name: a_code_set_after_the_first_sign_in_was_removed
vectors.why: The rule waits on the key the event named, though it was removed, so an owner who replaced their first device still sets the code.

vectors.name: a_code_committing_to_the_ids_sealing_key
vectors.why: Nor the sealing key, so whoever holds the reading key never holds the backup.

vectors.name: a_code_naming_no_code_again
vectors.why: The rule it sets is a real one, or the ID could stay without a code and take one rule statement after another.

vectors.name: a_rule_statement_with_another_version
vectors.why: v names its kind.

vectors.name: a_recovery_naming_no_code
vectors.why: Whoever recovers holds the code, so the next rule is a real one.

vectors.name: a_statement_for_another_id
vectors.why: A statement fits one ID.

vectors.name: a_key_statement_out_of_order
vectors.why: And one place in its chain, which counts every kind of statement.

vectors.name: a_stale_prev
vectors.why: A statement names the one before it, so one signed on an older head doesn't follow.

vectors.name: a_recovery_counting_only_recoveries
vectors.why: A recovery's seq counts every statement, key statements included.

vectors.name: an_addition_extends
vectors.why: A copy with more statements after the same ones counts.

vectors.name: an_older_copy_changes_nothing
vectors.why: A host can't bring a removed key back by showing an old copy.

vectors.name: two_key_only_branches_are_forked
vectors.why: Two of the owner's keys signed two branches, and nothing says which is real.

vectors.name: a_removed_keys_branch_is_forked
vectors.why: No key outranks another, so the removed key's branch is a fork, not a loss.

vectors.name: a_recovery_after_the_split_wins
vectors.why: The backup overrides any key, so the copy with a recovery after the split counts.

vectors.name: the_same_the_other_way_round
vectors.why: Whichever copy a reader held first.

vectors.name: rules_signed_by_an_added_key
vectors.why: A key added by one that counts signs at once.

vectors.name: rules_signed_by_a_removed_key
vectors.why: What arrives now is checked under the keys that count now.

vectors.name: rules_from_the_touch_that_added_their_key
vectors.why: The rules from the same touch verify alone, under the copy that has the addition.

vectors.name: an_approval_by_an_added_key
vectors.why: Every key that counts says yes for the owner.

vectors.name: an_approval_by_a_key_a_recovery_dropped
vectors.why: A recovery leaves only the key it names.

vectors.name: a_binding_naming_an_agent_with_a_key_statement
vectors.why: Only an owner's ID may have more than one key.

vectors.name: an_envelope_signed_by_a_key_an_agent_added
vectors.why: An ID with a key statement is an owner's, so nothing it signs as an agent counts, whichever key signed.

vectors.name: a_binding_by_the_agents_own_key_added_as_an_owners
vectors.why: Even then, a binding arriving now that the agent's own key signed as its owner is refused.

vectors.name: a_binding_by_a_key_recovered_from_one_that_added_the_agents
vectors.why: Nothing compares the two IDs' keys, so what was added before a recovery never holds the owner's recovered key back.

vectors.name: a_yes_by_the_agents_own_key_added_as_an_owners
vectors.why: Nor a yes arriving now whose delegation the agent's own key signed as its owner.

vectors.name: an_owners_yes_arriving_now
vectors.why: A sign-in that counts says yes for the owner.

vectors.name: an_owners_yes_by_the_agents_own_key_arriving_now
vectors.why: A yes arriving now that the agent's own key signed as its owner is refused, though only whoever holds that key outside Signet could have added it.

vectors.name: an_owners_yes_by_the_agents_own_key_read_back
vectors.why: Read back, a yes is taken as it was signed: nothing compares the two IDs' keys.

vectors.name: an_owners_yes_by_a_removed_sign_in_arriving_now
vectors.why: What arrives now is checked under the sign-ins that count now.

vectors.name: an_owners_yes_by_a_removed_sign_in_read_back
vectors.why: Read back, under every sign-in the owner has had.

vectors.name: a_delegates_yes_under_the_agents_own_key_read_back
vectors.why: And so is a delegate's, whose delegation the agent's own key signed.

vectors.name: a_chain_with_a_yes_by_a_key_recovered_from_one_that_added_the_agents
vectors.why: Once the owner recovers from it, the recovered key's yes counts.

vectors.name: a_binding_by_an_added_key
vectors.why: An added key binds an agent at once.

vectors.name: a_delegation_to_a_key_the_owner_had
vectors.why: A delegate's caps can't be skipped by naming a key the owner added, removed or not.

vectors.name: a_binding_read_back_after_its_key_was_removed
vectors.why: What a removed key signed before reads back, as an old key's does after a recovery.

vectors.name: a_binding_by_a_key_added_after_the_recovery_it_names
vectors.why: An object reads back only under the keys of the epoch it names.

vectors.name: a_binding_by_a_key_added_in_the_epoch_it_names
vectors.why: And under any of that epoch's keys.

vectors.name: a_binding_by_the_agents_own_key_read_back
vectors.why: What's read back is taken as it was signed, so a binding the agent's own key signed as its owner's sign-in reads back, though arriving now it's refused.

vectors.name: a_history_extended_past_a_recovery_on_a_copy_that_added_the_agents_key
vectors.why: An owner's recovery on top of a copy that added their agent's key still extends the agent's history, so its contacts still take its messages.
